transcript: I'm going on a West Coast theatre trip like. Like right now I'm at the airport and I realised I haven't really talked about it at all, so I should. So I'm about to fly to San Francisco, which is fun cause I have not been to San Francisco since I was like 19 maybe. And I'm going for three shows. First I'm seeing The Lunch Box at Berkeley Rep tonight. I'm very excited. I've never been to Berkeley Rep. This is a theatre that I've always wanted to visit because so many airports are loud. I've always wanted to go to Berkeley because they have so many shows that have ended up going to Broadway. like Galileo coming this fall. But the lunchbox is based on a movie by Ritesh Batra He is also writing the book of the musical. I've never seen it and my friend who is working on the show says to wait to watch the movie. until after I've seen the musical and the main reason I'm going is cause the music is written by the Lazour brothers who I love, I love. We live in Cairo, I love night side songs. So I just like had to see it. And it's directed by Rachel Chavkin, so I can't wait. I'm also seeing it on Wednesday for opening night. So yeah, I'm seeing it twice. And then tomorrow at the American Conservatory Theatre ACT In San Francisco I'm seeing Hamnet. If you saw the movie With Jesse Buckley and Paul Mescal. It's based off the same book by Maggie O'farrell. And this was the production that was at Royal Shakespeare Company, uh, in Stratford in the U K. I'm excited to see it. It's actually the closing performance, but ACT Is also a theatre I've always wanted to check out. So it's two new theatres in technically a new city, not a new state. cause i’ve seen shows in California. And then this is where it gets crazy. On Monday, I'm driving down the coast from San Francisco to Los Angeles, and I'm seeing Brigadoon on Tuesday. And I love Brigadoon so I would want to see it anyway. But this particular production is a rewritten book by Al Silber who I adore. I’ve seen Al in a lot of shows. I really love her work. I've never seen anything that she's written, so I can't wait to see this. And it's directed by Katie Spelman Katie Spelman was the choreographer on The Notebook. She's worked in a lot of theatre spaces. She also directed wonder, which I saw earlier this year and loved. so I bet her Brigadoon is going to be amazing. It's at Pasadena Playhouse, a theatre that I also really love. And then I'm driving back to San Francisco, so is it dumb? Maybe. Do I care? No. And then I fly back to New York on Thursday, so a little West Coast jaunt. Very excited. Let me know if You have any recs? Cause I've literally planned, um, nothing else.
classificationReason: Creator is announcing a West Coast theatre trip and previewing multiple shows (The Lunch Box at Berkeley Rep, at least one more).
